title: The cider barrel
logline: Tuesday. What he drew during the rehearsal week's first party: the artisanal cider barrel. Thirty times. From every side. The strip shows the sketchbook's pages and none of the people.

panels.composition: The pavilion's terrace, a party in blinding light. WOOD against a post with the sketchbook, drawing. Everyone else drawn as legs and glasses at the panel's edges.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a thin man in a dark suit leaning on a cedar post at a bright terrace party drawing in a sketchbook, other guests visible only as legs and raised glasses at the edges

panels.composition: The sketchbook page: the cider barrel, from the front. Twelve lines. Perfect.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, close-up of a sketchbook page with a precise twelve-line ink drawing of a wooden cider barrel on a stand

panels.composition: The next page: the barrel from the side. The next: the tap. The next: the barrel from above. Thirty drawings, drawn as a grid of small panels within the panel.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a panel subdivided into a grid of tiny precise ink drawings of the same cider barrel from thirty different angles
image.notes: Thirty barrels in one panel, as a grid. No people.

panels.composition: Wood closing the book. A GUEST (legs, a glass) asking what he's drawing.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a thin man closing a sketchbook while a guest visible only from the waist down holds a glass and asks a question

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: Thirty barrels. 'It's the only one here.'
